chunks: It has been narrated: “That the she-camel of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was outrun, so he عليه السلام said:”

“It transgressed and said: ‘Upon me is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.’ And it is a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that nothing transgresses against anything except that Allah abases it. And if a mountain were to transgress against a mountain, Allah would surely bring down the transgressing one of them.”

key_terms.الْبَاغِيَ: The transgressing one; the party that acts with wrongful excess.
key_terms.بَغَتْ: It transgressed or acted arrogantly beyond proper bounds.
key_terms.جَبَلًا: A mountain, used here as an example to illustrate the universal rule.
key_terms.حَقٌّ عَلَى اللَّهِ: A firmly established divine principle or decree from Allah.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about arrogance, transgression, and Allah’s humbling of the proud?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that arrogance and transgression lead to abasement, even when imagined in the case of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله she-camel. It presents a general divine principle: whatever exceeds its proper bounds and acts haughtily over another is humbled by Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ.
